label: Copy phase: about to output "g" right after echoing "i" (or "g"), i.e. the original bigram "i g"/"g g", from copy position 3 on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original or delimiter steps. All activations have input i (89% of mass) or g (11%). The output target is mostly g (78% of mass), so the feature tracks the original bigram "i g" being replayed: the step where the model has just echoed i and must now emit g. Weaker activations come from g->g (repeated g) and from i->i / i->j / i->2. The strongest examples are i->g at recall_idx 3-4. The i->g, recall_idx>=3 subset alone gets precision 0.93 with 65% of mass. It is almost silent when the pair falls at recall_idx 0-2 (early copy positions), and the false positives of the broader predicate are mostly g->g and some i->g steps that do not fire. It never fires on any other input token. Low-quartile activations are mostly i->i and g->g repeats.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=12: i, g; t=13: i, g; t=10: i, g) and the token being output (most: g, i, j, 2, b, p; least: v, c, d, 1); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=4 & t=6.
